description:
After JMAP-ic0j.68 closed the per-id /set Value-shaped leak, the JmapError-shaped top-level leak that JMAP-ic0j.53 nominally closed is STILL present at 5 sites:

  - crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/event.rs:884 — QueryCalendarEventsError::Other(e) in handle_calendar_event_query
  - crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/event.rs:996 — Err(e) in handle_calendar_event_set (likely ParseError or similar)
  - crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:1451 — BackendSetError -> JmapError::server_fail
  - crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:1531 — same

Each site calls .map_err(|e| JmapError::server_fail(e.to_string())) or returns Err(JmapError::server_fail(e.to_string())), bypassing server_fail_from_backend and leaking the backend Display text onto the wire as the method-level serverFail description.

The bd:JMAP-ic0j.53 memory entry explicitly documents the contract: 'the handler MUST map Other via server_fail_from_backend(&e) — NOT JmapError::server_fail(e.to_string()). The latter pattern leaks backend Display text to the wire and bypasses the workspace-wide redaction contract'.

Fix: at each site, replace JmapError::server_fail(e.to_string()) with server_fail_from_backend(&e). For sites without an existing 'use jmap_server::server_fail_from_backend' line, add the import.

Test pattern: same FAULTY_BACKEND_CANARY discipline from JMAP-ic0j.68, but targeting the top-level Invocation error path.

P1 leakage; should land as a workspace sweep mirroring JMAP-ic0j.68's structure. Found while working JMAP-ic0j.31.
title: Method-level JmapError::server_fail(e.to_string()) leak still present at 5 sites — JMAP-ic0j.53 anti-pattern
